speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the exact location of the pain in your right groin and how your leg is currently positioned? I also need to know if you are able to bear any weight on that leg at all.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is your right leg externally rotated and shortened compared to the left, and are you able to move your right ankle and toes? I need to assess for potential hip fracture or dislocation signs.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The posture of your right leg—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is classic for a posterior hip dislocation. I will immediately order imaging to confirm this and check for associated fractures. REQUEST TEST: Pelvis_X-Ray

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your right leg or foot? I need to rule out sciatic nerve injury, which is a common complication of posterior hip dislocations.

speaker: Patient
text: Alert and active. No head injury, abdominal pain, or chest pain reported.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming that you are alert and have no other injuries. Since the posterior hip dislocation is confirmed and there are no signs of associated fractures or neurological deficits, I am ready to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior hip dislocation
